Here is what I understand so far.

**What it's for.** The logbook replaces your notebook and your monthly retyping into the spreadsheet. You are the main reader. Your most common use is a quick check: "Have I worked this station before?" Once a year you export everything as ADIF (the standard log-exchange file format) and upload it to Logbook of The World (LoTW) to confirm contacts for awards.

**Scale and conditions.** About thirty contacts a week. You log at home and at field days. Sometimes you have no internet, so the logbook must work fully offline.

**My proposals (my calls, not yours yet):**
- It runs on a laptop and keeps the log in a local file you own. That covers field days without internet. It also keeps your data out of any service you don't control.
- Each contact records at least the fields LoTW needs: callsign, date and time in UTC, band or frequency, and mode. It also records the optional fields you write in your notebook today.
- The "worked before?" lookup shows results as you type a callsign. That makes it useful in the middle of a contact, not only afterward.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- LoTW does not take a raw ADIF upload. You sign the file with ARRL's TQSL program first. The logbook only needs to write a clean ADIF file. TQSL handles the signing.
- LoTW matches contacts on callsign, UTC time, band and mode. A small error in any of these silently costs a confirmation. So correct entry at log time matters more than export features.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

What's wrong or missing here, and in particular, would you type each contact into the logbook at the radio, or keep the paper notebook and enter them later?
